content_blocks.title: Apply the idea
content_blocks.text: Write the smallest DDL statement for this object, inspect its definition, and document a safe reset for the disposable lab. Write down the expected result before running the snippet. Compare actual output with the reference, then try one normal case and one edge case.

content_blocks.code:
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS codeleaf_mysql_lab;
SELECT SCHEMA_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA WHERE SCHEMA_NAME = 'codeleaf_mysql_lab';
content_blocks.expected_output: The information_schema query returns the lab schema name if it exists.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in a dedicated local MySQL lab using the stated MySQL release track. For schema-changing or administrative snippets, inspect every statement and use only a disposable schema; the in-page editor shows reference output and does not execute SQL.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Remove only objects created for this lesson from the disposable schema/session, or restore the lab snapshot. Never run reset or destructive commands against production.

content_blocks.title: Version, security, and safety note
content_blocks.text: Use MySQL 9.7 LTS documentation as the default stable-track reference; verify behavior against MySQL 26.7 documentation when relevant and label any MySQL 8.4-specific fact. Examples are static references, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run mutation, privilege, replication, backup, and recovery examples only in an isolated lab.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a sample result proves the whole design is correct.
common_mistakes.why: Edge cases such as NULLs, duplicate matches, concurrency, privileges, or version differences may change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a targeted boundary case and record the server version, schema and expected result.

common_mistakes.problem: Running a mutating or administrative example in the wrong environment.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data changes, access grants, and recovery commands may have persistent impact.
common_mistakes.fix: Use a disposable lab, preview targets and permissions, and write a reset/recovery plan before executing.
